 Adou Thiero (ankle) is questionable to play against the Suns on Sunday. 
 Thiero has been a rotation piece for the Lakers since making his season debut last Thursday. His status for this game is up in the air, and he could take on a larger role if he plays since Austin Reaves (heel) is out. Ziaire Williams would play extra minutes if Thiero is out.

 Austin Reaves (heel) has been ruled out against the Suns on Sunday. 
 Reaves exited early from Wednesday’s win, and he’ll remain out despite getting a few days off between games. Quentin Grimes will be back following a two-game absence and should get the starting nod with Reaves sidelined.

 Reaves is dealing with a heel bruise. The 28-year-old guard missed practice Saturday, though it’s unclear if he’ll miss any game time. 
 Austin Reaves 
 LAL 
 Guard 
 #15 
 ESPN’s Dave McMenamin reports that Austin Reaves is listed as day-to-day with a bruised heel. 
 According to head coach JJ Redick, Reaves and the Lakers medical staff opted against imaging. This latest update is favorable for the severity of the injury, and Reaves could miss little time, if any at all. If Reaves is forced to sit out, Collin Sexton and Quentin Grimes could pick up the slack. 
 Luka Dončić 
 LAL 
 Forward-Guard 
 #77 
 Luka Dončić (ankle) finished Wednesday’s win over the Bucks with 32 points (10-of-25 FGs, 7-of-10 FTs), five rebounds, five assists, three steals and five three-pointers. 
 Dončić has scored at least 30 points in each of his last nine appearances. However, there was a concerning moment when the Lakers star appeared to tweak his ankle during the fourth quarter. The benches were being cleared at this point, so Dončić returned to the Lakers’ locker room with a team trainer with 4:23 remaining in the fourth quarter. We’ll see if he lands on the injury report for Friday’s game against the Spurs, especially with Austin Reaves (heel) leaving Wednesday’s victory during the third quarter.

 The Lakers were already up double digits, so there was no need to bring him back in. If he is to miss time, look for Collin Sexton to take more shots and more minutes for Quentin Grimes. They both become stream options in redraft leagues but not high priority ones.

 HoopsHype’s Michael Scotto reports that the Hawks are signing Rafael Castro to a two-way contract. 
 After going undrafted this past summer, Castro signed an Exhibit 10 contract with the Rockets in late September. Waived on October 1, the former George Washington center signed an Exhibit 10 deal with the Lakers on October 9, then was waived eight days later. Given the Hawks’ frontcourt injuries, Castro gives them another option to call on if needed. To open a two-way slot for him, the Hawks are waiving injured guard Keshon Gilbert.
